heading: Pick a model by what you care about
mobileHint: Tap or drag the triangle to set your priorities.
mapDescription: A triangle of hexagons. Each corner puts all 12 units on Smart, Time or Cost. Each colour shows the top model for that mix. Use the arrow keys to move between hexagons and Enter to pick one.
donorRule: + takes a quarter unit from the largest other axis. − gives a quarter unit to the largest other axis. The three always add up to 12.
decreaseTitle: Give a quarter unit to the largest other axis
increaseTitle: Take a quarter unit from the largest other axis
caption: {count} frontier models · top: {top}
explainRanking: The page ranks models in two steps. First it drops every model that another model matches or beats on every axis you gave power to. The models left over form the Pareto frontier. An axis with zero power plays no part in this step or the next.
Then it sorts the frontier by interquartile minimax regret, using your allocation as the weights. The model whose worst case is least bad comes first.

Each hexagon is one way to split the 12 units in whole steps, and its colour is the model that ranks first there. Click or tap a hexagon to use its split. Drag across the triangle to move in quarter units. The table above lists the frontier for the current split. The ring marks the current split, which can sit between hexagons.
explainRegret: For each axis, a model's regret is how far it sits from the best value on the frontier. That gap is divided by the interquartile range of the axis across the frontier, so a gap counts as big or small relative to how spread out the frontier is. Time uses a log scale, so halving the time counts the same whether a task takes ten seconds or ten minutes.

Each axis's regret is then multiplied by that axis's share of the 12 units. A model's score is its largest weighted regret, and ties go to the lower mean weighted regret. The lowest score wins. With all 12 units on one axis, the frontier shrinks to the models that are best on that axis.
Put simply, the top model is the one that is never far behind on anything you care about.
explainMetricsTitle: How Smart, Time and Cost are measured
explainMetricsIntro: Every number comes straight from the catalog, with no adjustment by this page.
explainData: This page uses {name}, version {version}, generated on {date}.
explainEmbedded: The page carries a stripped copy of the catalog: each model's name, creator, release date and three metrics. It makes no network requests, so it works offline and sends nothing anywhere. Rebuild the page to pick up new data.
footerMethod: Pareto frontier over the axes with power, then interquartile minimax regret.
